extracted.intended_audience: poets, dramatists, critics, dancing-masters, and educated readers interested in composition and theatrical performance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for composing and judging sublime epic battle-scenes, dramatic performance, and the art of dancing — emphasizing imagination, judgment, classical models, pacing, clarity, and decorum. Also addresses how small technical accomplishments (gesture, deportment) affect larger talents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare the reader's expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise the reader's expectation and prepare them for a great scene by foreshadowing it in preceding passages (e.g., Milton "raised his Readers Expectation, and prepared him for it by several Passages in the preceding Books").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use earlier passages to ready the imagination so the main scene feels earned; reserve and arrange prior hints deliberately (the author notes omitting certain quotations until the opening of the Book).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime imagination — 'rise above himself'
rubrics_metrics.description: When treating sublime subjects, the poet should expand his imagination to its utmost: "wherever he speaks of it, he rises, if possible, above himself."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy elevated language and loftier flights of imagination for the greatest actions; let diction and imagery scale with subject-matter to produce astonishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of judgment to avoid the mean or trivial
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine expansive imagination with exactness of judgment to "avoid every thing that might appear light or trivial."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject images or incidents that slide into burlesque or puerility; keep grandeur free of ridiculous detail that would undermine the sublime effect (contrast Milton's restraint with Claudian's wanton images).

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitate the ancients but improve upon them
rubrics_metrics.description: Make use of the helps found among ancient poets while improving what is sublime and rejecting what is puerile: "Milton... has taken every thing that is sublime in these several Passages, and composes out of them... without its Puerilities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borrow effective classical motifs (Homer, Virgil, scripture) but adapt and refine them rather than copying their faults; take the best traits and recompose them into superior images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradation and escalation in battle scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure martial engagements so they rise one above another and escalate in horror and grandeur (Homer's battles "still rising one above another").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design successive encounters with increasing intensity and variety (e.g., first engagement under a cope of fire, second with artificial thunders, then mountain-tearing, then the climactic appearance of the Messiah).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use images appropriate to the subject's scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Select signs and images befitting the nature of the action—e.g., the Battle of Angels is "usher'd in with such Signs of Wrath as are suitable to Omnipotence incensed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the magnitude of metaphor and spectacle (thunder, lightning, chariots, earthquakes) to the theological or mythic stature of characters to preserve verisimilitude of tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify bold inventions by internal plausibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Bold or unexpected devices (e.g., attributing the first use of artillery to rebel angels) may be permissible if they fit the character and aims of those agents: "it was certainly a very bold Thought... but... it entered very properly into the Thoughts of that Being..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When introducing unusual elements, provide internal rationale or precedent so they seem natural within the poem's logic; avoid arbitrary novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid burlesque; keep terror from becoming ridicule
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain horror without lapsing into ridicule or burlesque (contrast Homer/Claudian's excesses with Milton's restraint: Claudian's island-throwing "savour more of Burlesque").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject grotesque or extravagant conceits that divert rather than astonish; preserve the audience's awe by tempering extravagance with dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer specific, significant particulars when they enlarge the idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific named particulars (Homer naming Pelion, Ossa, Olympus) can swell an image and add grandeur; use particularity when the scene furnishes it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ well-chosen proper names and concrete particulars to deepen the reader's imaginative conception, but only when they enhance rather than distract from the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide resting-places to aid reader attention and pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermix great action with "Speeches, Reflections, Similitudes, and the like Reliefs" to give the reader opportunities to recover and thus enhance the effect of the nobler parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate intense description with reflective or dialogic passages to vary the tempo; pacing and relief preserve attention and make grand passages more effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scriptural and poetical allusions to enrich rather than overwhelm
rubrics_metrics.description: Allusions to scripture and prior poets (e.g., Messiah's chariot from Ezekiel; the sword-gift motif from Virgil) can heighten effect when appropriately integrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw on authoritative precedents to deepen resonance, ensuring they cohere with the poem's theology and imagery rather than appearing as mere ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve coherent rules for the supernatural within the poem
rubrics_metrics.description: When representing non-mortal beings, establish consistent qualities (e.g., celestial wounds produce 'nectarous Humour'—"such as celestial Spirits may bleed").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and adhere to a consistent metaphysical logic for supernatural entities (how they wound, bleed, recover) so striking episodes remain credible within the poem's universe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small technical accomplishments (deportment, gesture) matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'good Mein' (becoming Motion, Gesture and Aspect) can make even naturally gifted persons more agreeable; small attainments confirm and heighten natural advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate gesture, carriage, and composure as part of a writer's or performer's craft; technical polish amplifies larger talents and improves audience perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codify fundamental rules to improve practice and judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Dancing (by analogy, any art) should have 'fundamental Rules, that might so tend to the Improvement of its Professors, and Information of the Spectators.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear standards and instructional principles so practitioners can improve and audiences can judge with informed taste; formalizing basics elevates the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity and appropriate decorum in stage movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage dancing should avoid being supplanted by 'Capering and Tumbling' and should retain the elegance and regularity befitting theatrical and social use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor measured, decorous movement appropriate to character and context; ensure spectacle does not devolve into base acrobatics when the art requires grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and descriptive grounding of form and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: An account of antiquity, the particular dances, and the masters is part of a sound treatise: describe origin, nature, and perfection of parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and teach the historical forms and functions of techniques—knowledge of past practice informs present refinement and preserves useful distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek principles of proportion and order (aspire to regular science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion and dancing may be reducible to orderly principles (analogy to Pythagoras discovering musical ratios): 'Who knows therefore but Motion... may not... be reduced into a regular Science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for measurable principles (timing, proportion, harmony) that can systematize practice and allow objective evaluation and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of speech and intelligibility in tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Actors in tragedy should 'talk to be understood'—clarity of language is a criterion for good dramatic writing and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure dialogue and delivery preserve intelligibility; poetic elevation should not obscure meaning so much that the audience cannot follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical expression must fit and convey character
rubrics_metrics.description: Majestic conceptions should be expressed in movement: 'majestick and great Conceptions are expressed in the very Step' (example: Booth's Pyrrhus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align gait, gesture, and posture with psychological and social profile of characters; physicality should communicate character as decisively as words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement and emotional investment as measures of success
rubrics_metrics.description: A play or performance should engage its audience so spectators feel concern and curiosity about outcomes (Sir Roger's sustained attention and puzzlement over the plot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create characters and situations that provoke attentive sympathy or curiosity; the audience's sustained emotional involvement indicates effective composition and staging.
